illegal_when_clauses.clause: order = message, then FACTS, then actions, then what-happens-next

per_role.definition: One number the reader takes away, optionally with its movement. The tile a dashboard's top row is made of.
per_role.axis: FFF: function "how big is it, and did it move?"

providers.json_when: default — label · value · delta · period, no series
providers.meta_when: shape = one-measure × value-and-delta AND series = none AND delta != none — the default of the role; beats kpi-tile (roles.json when: "a series exists to show (s247-D3 / DP-08: no series ⇒ not a KPI tile)") exactly when no series exists, and beats Chart-bullet (when: "a target or performance band is the point, not the delta") when the delta, not a band, is the claim.

providers.json_when: a series exists to show (s247-D3 / DP-08: no series ⇒ not a KPI tile)
providers.meta_when: shape = one-measure × value-delta-and-series AND series != none — beats stat-card (roles.json when: "default — label · value · delta · period, no series") whenever a series exists to show; yields to Chart-bullet (when: "a target or performance band is the point, not the delta") when target != none, and to runway-bar (when: "the number is 'money vs what is already scheduled'") when the measure is money-vs-scheduled.

providers.json_when: a target or performance band is the point, not the delta
providers.meta_when: answers=comparison AND the reading is one measure against a target plus qualitative performance bands AND span.cols 4–6 — beats stat-card (60, "default — label · value · delta · period, no series") and kpi-tile (50, "a series exists to show") when the BENCHMARK, not the delta and not a series, is the point; yields to both when no target exists.

providers.json_when: the number is "money vs what is already scheduled"
providers.meta_when: answers = one-number AND shape = one-measure × committed-vs-balance-split AND verdict != none — beats stat-card (60, "default — label · value · delta · period, no series") and kpi-tile (50, "a series exists to show") when the reading is "money vs what is already scheduled" and the takeaway is a VERDICT WITH A DATE rather than a delta or a trend; yields to stat-card when there is nothing committed to net off, to kpi-tile when a series is the claim, and to Chart-bullet (40, "a target or performance band is the point, not the delta") when a target band, not a coverage date, is the benchmark.

per_role.definition: A count or state against a threshold. The DESK example role, kept as named.
per_role.axis: FFF: function "how many, against what, and is that fine?"

providers.json_when: one state, one dot + label, 2–4 cols
providers.meta_when: shape = one-state × dot-and-label AND span.cols <= 4 — the default of the role; beats summary (roles.json when: "n × count as a key/value list, 6–12 cols") whenever exactly one state is read; yields to badge (when: "inline, attached to another element, count only") when the dot is attached to another element rather than standing alone.

providers.json_when: n × count as a key/value list, 6–12 cols
providers.meta_when: shape = rows × name-value-pairs AND rows >= 2 AND span.cols >= 6 — beats status-indicator (roles.json when: "one state, one dot + label, 2–4 cols") whenever more than one row must be read at once; yields to meter (when: "the threshold is a cap being spent against (limits-meter reading)") when threshold = cap-spent-against, and to badge (when: "inline, attached to another element, count only") when the reading is inline.

providers.json_when: the threshold is a cap being spent against (limits-meter reading)
inline, attached to another element, count only

per_role.definition: A charted reading in a panel. ONE role for all fourteen charts: the five intent words (comparison · change-over-time · distribution · relationship · composition) already live on the answers axis (chart-intents.json, s251-D11), so they gate; the role only names the slot. Five roles named after the intents would duplicate that axis and break "three independent axes" (s251-D3). This is the call most worth striking if you disagree — see §14 call 1.
per_role.axis: FFF: function is the chart-intent word, gated by answers, not by the role

providers.json_when: comparison; stacked variant when composition across categories
providers.meta_when: answers = comparison AND axis.x = categorical — beats chart-line (roles.json when: "change-over-time") when the x-dimension is categorical rather than a time continuum, and beats chart-pie (when: "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts") when the parts do not sum to a whole; the stacked variant takes composition across categories, where it yields to chart-stacked-area (when: "composition over time") if the axis is time.

answers=change-over-time AND series 1–5 on ONE continuous time axis AND axes=present AND span.cols ≥ 6 — the role's default at this intent, and it beats every sibling whose own `when` adds a further condition; yields to chart-combo (56, "two measures in different units over one axis") when units differ, to Chart-candlestick (44, "OHLC per period") when all four price points per period are the claim, and to chart-sparkline (30, "inline scale, no axes") when span.cols < 6.

providers.json_when: composition, a centre total is meaningful
providers.meta_when: answers=composition AND parts sum to a whole AND total=printed as a centre figure — beats chart-pie (48, "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts") whenever the total is worth printing, and beats it on nothing else; yields to chart-stacked-area (64, "composition over time") when the split MOVES.

answers = distribution AND variables = 1 AND bins = contiguous (no inter-bar gap) AND baseline = 0 — roles.json when: "distribution, one variable"; beats Chart-boxplot (roles.json: "distribution per category") when the frequency shape of ONE variable is the claim; yields to Chart-boxplot when categories >= 2; the no-gap rule is not cosmetic — the FT gives the same reason: "keep the gaps between columns small to highlight the 'shape' of the data".

answers=relationship AND both axes carry quantitative measures — the ONLY provider of relationship in the role, so it beats every sibling on the answers gate alone and needs no further test; yields to chart-combo (56) when the two measures share one x axis in different units instead of being plotted against each other. span.cols max 8 because a runtime fit is not baked (this meta's own responsive rule).

answers spans change-over-time AND composition AND cumulative bands share ONE total across the time axis — beats chart-donut (80, "composition, a centre total is meaningful") and chart-pie (48) when the split MOVES rather than being a snapshot; yields to chart-line (88, "change-over-time") when the total is not meaningful.

answers = distribution AND categories >= 2 AND each category carries a five-number summary AND span.cols <= 8 — roles.json when: "distribution per category"; beats Chart-histogram (roles.json: "distribution, one variable") whenever the spread must be read PER CATEGORY; yields to it when variables = 1 and the bin shape is the claim.

providers.json_when: two measures in different units over one axis
providers.meta_when: answers=change-over-time AND series=2 AND units=different AND both read against ONE shared x (dv-line-006) — beats chart-line (88, "change-over-time") on the different-units test and on nothing else; yields to chart-line (multi-series) or chart-bar (grouped) for a same-unit pair, which this meta's own antiPattern forbids drawing as a combo.

answers=comparison AND series=2 mirrored outward from a shared centre gutter AND categories ≥ 6 — beats chart-bar (grouped) when the two series must read as OPPOSED directions rather than adjacent columns; yields to Chart-butterfly-v (36, "as above, wide panel") when the category axis is ordered left-to-right and span.cols ≥ 8.

answers=comparison AND series=2 mirrored above/below ONE horizontal baseline AND the category axis is ordered left-to-right (time, rank) AND span.cols ≥ 8 — yields to Chart-butterfly-h (40, "exactly two series mirrored, categories ≥ 6") whenever the categories are unordered or the panel is narrower than 8 cols; both yield to chart-bar for an ordinary grouped comparison.

answers=composition AND parts ≤ 5 AND total=not printed — yields to chart-donut (80, "composition, a centre total is meaningful") whenever a centre total is wanted, which is the only thing separating the two; yields to chart-stacked-area (64) when the split moves over time.

answers = change-over-time AND shape = periods × OHLC (open · high · low · close per session) — roles.json when: "OHLC per period"; beats chart-line (roles.json: "change-over-time") only when all four price points per period are the claim; yields to chart-line whenever one measure's path is enough.

per_role.definition: Many records of one kind, one per row. Shape splits it: columns, cards, ledger lines, time-ordered.

providers.json_when: sort / filter / select / edit-in-place is required
the records are a ledger with a running balance
the records are issued documents to open / download
the records are future recurring instructions
time is the structure, records have happened
providers.meta_when: records >= 2 AND time IS the structure AND every record has ALREADY HAPPENED AND entries are not buttons AND order is newest-first with date headings — roles.json when: "time is the structure, records have happened"; beats list-items when the date rail is the reading rather than a sort order; yields to list-items inside a date group the moment entries must open (our AP1), and never borrows Progress-tracker's aria-current because there is no current step (our AP0).

per_role.definition: The shell around everything. Seven providers, one per frame; only one can win, so not-with is implicit among co-providers (Debian: one-at-a-time facility).
per_role.axis: FFF: form dominates — the frame is chosen by navigation depth and job

providers.json_when: default for dashboards (the bento template composes it)
providers.meta_when: destinations <= 7 AND nav.levels <= 2 — the default for dashboards — the bento template composes it; beats app-shell-side-nav (roles.json when: "> 7 destinations or two nav levels") below those bounds and app-shell-nav-rail (when: "dense app, content cannot spare 248px") when the content can spare the column; yields to app-shell-multi-column (when: "list-and-detail job") and to app-shell-focused (when: "one job, no navigation (auth, wizard)") when the job has no navigation. Co-providers of page-frame are mutually exclusive by construction (roles.json §05: one-at-a-time facility), so no not-with is authored.

providers.json_when: two peers on screen at once

providers.meta_when: primaryNavigation = absent AND breadcrumbs = absent AND search = absent AND exits = 1 AND job.count = 1 — the only frame defined by removal; beats every other shell (roles.json: all six carry navigation) whenever abandoning the task is the failure mode — authentication, a wizard, a passcode; yields to app-shell-top-nav the moment the user must be able to go somewhere else.

providers.json_when: marketing / servicing site with a mega-footer

per_role.definition: The band that names the page or a section of it. Providers differ by level, so when is the level.
per_role.axis: FFF: function "what am I looking at?"

providers.json_when: page level, with actions or tabs
page or screen level, app-only, no lock-up needed
providers.meta_when: level in (page, screen, section) AND platform = app AND lockup = none — yields to page-header-lockup (roles.json when: "page level, with actions or tabs") whenever actions or tabs ride the band; beats section-heading-lockup (when: "section level, above one board / table / panel") because the Header Section Titles type covers the section level app-side, and beats eyebrow (when: "a kicker alone is enough (rare; normally a part of the above)") whenever a title, not a kicker, is wanted.

providers.json_when: section level, above one board / table / panel
a kicker alone is enough (rare; normally a part of the above)

per_role.definition: Navigation that is not the frame. Global, local, in-page and mobile are the when values.
per_role.axis: FFF: function "where am I, where can I go?"

providers.meta_when: shape = destination-set × links AND scope = global — the default of the role; beats breadcrumbs (roles.json when: "ancestry, depth ≥ 2") and tabs (when: "local — peer views in one context") because those are ancestry and local peers, not the global set; yields to sidebar-nav (when: "global, desktop, persistent column (pairs with app-shell-side-nav)") when the page-frame is app-shell-side-nav, and to tab-bar (when: "mobile bottom, 3–5 destinations") on mobile.

providers.json_when: global, desktop, persistent column (pairs with app-shell-side-nav)
local — peer views in one context

providers.meta_when: shape = ancestor-path × links AND depth >= 2 — beats anchor-nav (roles.json when: "in-page, long document") when the trail is ancestry rather than in-page position; yields to navigations (when: "global — masthead / main-nav family") for global movement and to tabs (when: "local — peer views in one context") for peer views — it answers where-am-i, they answer where-can-i-go, so it complements rather than replaces them.

per_role.definition: A trigger. Emphasis (primary / secondary / ghost) is a placement property, not a role — Material's emphasis axis, per the DESK page.

providers.meta_when: emphasis in (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary) AND label = text — the default of the role; yields to icon-button (roles.json when: "space is tight and the glyph is universal") when label = glyph, to split-button (when: "one main action plus a menu of related ones") when a menu hangs off the action, and to links (when: "the action is navigation inside running text") when the action is navigation in prose.

providers.json_when: space is tight and the glyph is universal
providers.meta_when: the control performs an action AND space is tight OR the glyph is universal AND an accessible name is supplied AND the hit target is at least 44x44 AND a tooltip carries the label — CANON on the first half (roles.json: "space is tight and the glyph is universal"); beats button only where the glyph is unambiguous — our own meta: "Use a labelled Button when the action is not unambiguous from a glyph alone"; the tooltip is not optional company: Atlassian ("Use tooltips with icon buttons to display the button label") and Polaris ("Be provided for icon-only buttons") both make it a requirement, which our meta states only as an antiPattern.

providers.json_when: one main action plus a menu of related ones
the action is navigation inside running text
a row / grid of 4–8 shortcuts on an overview
a flow's primary + secondary pinned to the footer
marketing band, heading + support line + pair

per_role.definition: Containers and grids that hold other providers. The bento band itself is NOT here: its reflow / compress alternatives are owned by the band (s251-D14, rule 6b) and are not component-provided roles.
per_role.axis: FFF: form — these carry no content of their own

providers.json_when: default — container / stack / row / grid / twelve-column / split / measure
providers.meta_when: content = arbitrary-blocks AND surface = none — the default of the role; beats cards (roles.json when: "a bordered surface per item") whenever the arrangement must paint nothing, and beats stats-band-lockup (when: "3–6 headline-metrics in a labelled row") whenever the blocks are not headline-metrics; yields to divider (when: "a rule alone") when a rule alone is the whole need.

providers.json_when: one of a set at a time

per_role.definition: Status from the system to the person: persistence and placement are the when. Includes the nothing-yet states.
per_role.axis: FFF: function "the system is telling you something"

providers.meta_when: the message is IN FLOW (inside the page or form it refers to) AND it persists until resolved or dismissed AND it carries a status glyph and a title, never colour alone AND an error alert never auto-dismisses — CANON-ADJACENT — our own purpose already states the three-way rule: "Use Toast for transient confirmations and Banner for page-level persistent messages; use inline field validation (Input-fields) for single-control errors"; beats toast (proposed "transient, no answer required") whenever the reader must act; beats banner (proposed "the condition governs the whole page or session") whenever the message belongs to one form or section — Atlassian draws the identical line: "For messages with information affecting the whole site, use a banner"; yields to inline field validation for a single control.

providers.json_when: the RAG family in its four placements
a region has nothing to show
content is on its way, shape known
a task underway, full = done (meter's progress reading)

per_role.definition: The person gives a value. Provider chosen by value type; this role is large and will want sub-roles when forms get authored — not now.
per_role.axis: Not in the first pass (s251-D12) — listed so the library is whole

providers.meta_when: entry = free text AND expected answer fits ONE line AND no fixed option list exists AND the value is not money, a date, a time or a secret — the default text-entry field; beats textarea (proposed "the answer may span multiple lines") whenever the answer is a name, a reference or a phone number; yields to amount-input when the value is money, to date-picker / time-picker when it is a date or time, to secure-entry when it is a one-time code or PIN, and to dropdown or combobox whenever the answer must come from a list at all (Carbon: free text there "is likely to result in an error").

entry = free text AND the answer may run to more than one line AND there is no fixed option list AND a length limit is shown only where a real limit exists — beats input-fields (proposed "the answer fits one line") the moment a sentence is expected rather than a value — notes to approvers, a reason for payment, a secure message body; yields to input-fields for anything shorter (GOV.UK, verbatim: "enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number"); the counter is added only when a limit genuinely exists (GOV.UK: "Only use the character count component when there is a good reason for limiting").

NEVER — superseded 2026-07-24; the view switch is Segmented-control — carries no selection criterion because it is not a choice any composer should make: filter-toolbar-bar's AP1 already says "Consuming View-options instead of Segmented-control for the view switch — View-options was superseded"; the honest `when` here is a redirect, not a predicate.

per_role.definition: Something on top of the page that the person must dismiss or answer.
per_role.axis: Not in the first pass — listed so the library is whole

providers.json_when: a message or side-task that needs an answer

providers.meta_when: the content is STRUCTURED and FOCUSABLE AND it opens on CLICK from a labelled trigger AND it does not scroll AND it is non-modal (no focus trap, no aria-modal) AND only one is open — CANON-ADJACENT — our purpose already carries the three-way rule: "If the user can act inside it, it is a Popover; if it is a sentence of help text, it is a Tooltip; if it must interrupt, it is a Modal"; Atlassian states both halves independently ("For interactive overlays, use the modal dialog component" / "For non-essential, non-interactive messages, use the tooltip component"); yields to drawer or modals once the content scrolls (our antiPatterns[2], Atlassian: "Don't make popups that scroll", Carbon: past four columns wide use a modal).

providers.json_when: show a thing, not ask a thing
